seo.title: Who Owns Anduril? Stock, Investors & IPO (2026)
seo.description: Anduril remains privately owned at a $61B financing valuation. I examine its investors, IPO status and restrictions on stock transfers.

card.label: May 2026 valuation
card.alt: Anduril is privately owned; its May 2026 financing valued the company at $61 billion.

takeaways: May 13, 2026: a $5B Series H financing established a $61B headline valuation.
June 2025: Founders Fund invested $1B in the $2.5B Series G round, according to Reuters.
There is no public Anduril ticker established in the records checked on October 11, 2026.
A secondary stock quote does not establish permission to transfer the underlying shares.
changed: The latest priced company announcement I verified is the [May 13 Series H release](source:anduril-h). Thrive and a16z led the financing. A large private financing can extend the period during which a business funds itself without an exchange listing; it does not start an IPO countdown.

I separate that financing from the supplied lead about discussions near $100B. I have not substantiated a closing at that higher price in the records used for this article, so it is absent from the chart. A prospective price should replace the benchmark only when its event, terms and completion are documented.
ownership: This holder table is an evidence map, not a reconstructed cap table. Naming a fund as a round lead establishes participation at that date. It does not reveal all holdings bought earlier, secondary purchases, shares sold later or a current percentage. I retain the source dates beside each name.

[Reuters’ June 2025 account](source:anduril-g) connects Founders Fund to early backing and identifies Trae Stephens as both a cofounder and a fund partner. An overlapping person connects two institutions; it does not make them the same legal owner. I do not aggregate his undisclosed personal shares with fund holdings.

extras.heading: Who can actually transfer Anduril stock?
paragraphs: The practical ownership question is whether a buyer receives an interest the company recognizes. Anduril’s [investor-relations policy](source:anduril-ir) describes consent requirements and rights of first refusal affecting many shares. The seller’s contract with a buyer is only one part of the process.

My read: an offer page needs to disclose what is being sold. Direct shares, a vehicle holding shares and a contract promising future proceeds create different chains of ownership. The issuer, registered holder, administrator and buyer may be different parties. A pre-IPO label cannot resolve those differences.

I would check the issuing entity, security class, registered holder, consent conditions, fees, distribution waterfall and exit rights in the actual instrument. I have not reviewed a particular retail offering here. The company policy cannot establish that every intermediary product has identical legal or economic terms.

extras.heading: What $5 billion of new capital actually tells us
paragraphs: The 2021, 2025 and 2026 observations describe transactions at $4.6B, $30.5B and $61B. My calculation puts the last value at roughly 13.3 times the first. That is a comparison of company-level transaction benchmarks across different dates, not a return earned by every shareholder. Share classes, dilution, subsequent purchases and transfer restrictions can produce very different outcomes for individual investors.

If the $61B headline is read as a post-money equity value, $5B divided by $61B is approximately 8.2%. That is a simplifying new-money ratio, not a verified ownership allocation. The release does not give each fund’s subscription, identify secondary sales or supply the fully diluted capitalization used for pricing. I therefore keep Thrive and a16z’s current stakes marked undisclosed.

A secondary-market seller may quote a price for a particular instrument. To compare it with these funding values, I would need the number of shares, the class, contractual preferences and whether the company recognizes the transfer. Anduril’s transfer policy makes that last question especially material: a quoted economic exposure and valid registered ownership can be different things.

For the IPO question, a larger financing can extend a private company’s options without fixing a listing date. I would update this investigation when a company announcement, public registration document or completed corporate transaction changes those options. A new headline suggesting a higher valuation belongs in the reported-talks category until there is evidence that the transaction happened.

founderStory: The [2019 investor account](source:anduril-2019) gives a more useful starting point than the latest valuation. It names Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Matt Grimm, Joe Chen and Trae Stephens, linking their experience to Oculus, Palantir, military technology and defense investing. That combination explains how a hardware-and-software company could approach government customers while raising venture capital.

Andreessen Horowitz described a model in which Anduril financed development before selling products to government. I treat that as the investor’s description of its business model, rather than an audited conclusion about every contract. The ownership implication is straightforward: venture shareholders bear business exposure while procurement customers buy equipment and services. A government contract does not itself make the government a shareholder.

Luckey is a prominent founder; the latest financing letter identifies Schimpf as CEO. Neither fact establishes a personal ownership percentage. I apply the same distinction in [who owns Cursor](/who-owns-cursor/), where founder roles, investor backing and customers answer different questions. Individual wealth requires evidence beyond the value of the entire business.
funding: New capital and the price attached to the whole company are different quantities. Neither is the founder’s net worth. A founder estimate needs a substantiated stake, security rights, liabilities and actual liquidity. The financing benchmark alone supplies none of those missing inputs.

The May funding amount divided by the headline valuation is about 8.2%. That is a rough financing-size ratio, not Thrive’s stake or exact dilution. Preferred rights, option-pool changes and any secondary component can change what an individual holder owns. Share documents are needed to convert that ratio into a cap-table percentage.

A financing price is also specific to a transaction. It is not an issuer promise to buy all shares at that value. Different securities may have liquidation preferences, vesting or transfer conditions. A secondary buyer must reconcile its own terms with the rights behind the funding headline rather than assuming complete equivalence.
files.chartRead: I count three dated priced observations, rising from $4.6B in 2021 to $61B in 2026, about 13.3 times. The 2025-to-2026 benchmark doubles. The logarithmic event bars show ratios, not daily stock prices or returns on a particular share class.

finding.heading: The forward-contract clause matters more than the quoted price
paragraphs: The policy warns that forward contracts can interact with rights allowing the company to repurchase shares at their original purchase price. That makes the mechanics of a purported retail interest central to what a buyer might receive.

A high secondary quote is therefore insufficient evidence of realizable value. An investor needs to understand how issuer restrictions, repurchase rights and vehicle distributions interact before assuming that a contract tracks an eventual IPO price. I cannot calculate the result for an agreement I have not read.

This is independent analysis of a public document, not a claim to exclusive knowledge of private terms. Its application depends on the actual holder and security. It adds a checkable question to the article rather than repeating a speculative listing date.

leadership.since: Confirmed May 2026; appointment date not established here

stock: No ordinary exchange-listed Anduril share is established by the records reviewed. A broker search result, token reference or indicative secondary price does not supply a public ticker. Our [AI companies index](/ai-companies/) keeps company metrics beside their dates and definitions.

The listing checks are concrete: a public offering document, an admitted security, the issuer and the offered share class. A confidential submission could exist without a public document; this review does not establish that none exists. I have no verified IPO date to put on a calendar.

Investors researching private infrastructure face similar classification problems in [Crusoe’s ownership file](/who-owns-crusoe/) and [Lambda’s funding investigation](/who-owns-lambda/). Completed equity, an anticipated closing and a reported future financing should produce different labels in every comparison.

A private transfer may be possible in particular circumstances, but requires attention to issuer restrictions and the exact instrument. This review does not establish a public Anduril ticker.

This article does not validate a particular offering. Check who owns the underlying security, whether the transfer is recognized and how proceeds reach the buyer.

seo.title: Who Owns Groq? Nvidia Deal, Stock & IPO (2026)
seo.description: Groq remains independent. Nvidia’s filing records $13B paid plus $4B payable, with no equity purchased. I examine what that means for owners.

card.label: Licence payment schedule
card.alt: Groq remains independently owned; Nvidia disclosed $13 billion paid and $4 billion payable for licensing and hiring.

takeaways: December 2025: Nvidia licensed technology and hired personnel, without buying Groq equity in this transaction.
February 2026 filing: $13B paid and $4B payable, inclusive of imputed interest.
September 2025: Groq raised $750M at a $6.9B post-money financing valuation.
A $17B licence payment schedule is not a new company financing valuation.
changed: I opened [Nvidia’s FY2026 annual report](source:nvidia-10k) and compared its Groq note with the [December company announcement](source:groq-license). Together they give a more precise ownership answer than a headline calling this a takeover.

Technology rights and personnel moved into Nvidia’s orbit while Groq described an independent business and continuing GroqCloud. The remaining company’s assets, strategy and earnings potential therefore need a fresh examination. The old fundraising price cannot simply be relabeled an exit price.
ownership: The investor table dates participation to the September financing. It does not disclose a full post-licensing shareholder register. The founder’s departure does not establish whether he retained shares, sold them or received distributions.

Licensing technology is contractual permission; buying stock is ownership of an entity. Hiring a team, purchasing equipment and obtaining rights can change competitive economics without creating a corporate parent. The [Ownership archive](/category/ownership/) keeps those distinctions visible.

The current [privacy policy](source:groq-privacy) names Groq LLC, while Nvidia’s transaction filing identifies Groq, Inc. I preserve that distinction rather than assuming both documents describe the same corporate form on the same date. The policy’s displayed effective date does not establish when a conversion occurred.

extras.heading: Is Groq owned by Nvidia?
paragraphs: The reviewed transaction did not acquire Groq’s shares. Nvidia says it purchased no equity interests, customer contracts or existing products. That answers the scope of this transaction, rather than asserting that the parties could never have other financial relationships.

Non-exclusive rights are another separate dimension. That description does not reveal every constraint on future development or every retained intellectual-property right. I have not obtained the executed agreement and do not reconstruct provisions absent from the public statements.

This distinction also matters in [who owns ChatGPT and OpenAI](/who-owns-chatgpt-openai/). Commercial access to technology and ownership of its developer require separate records, even when the commercial relationship is large enough to reshape both businesses.

extras.heading: Why the old valuation does not price today’s Groq
paragraphs: The [2024 company financing announcement](source:groq-d) names BlackRock-managed funds and accounts as the lead, with Neuberger Berman, Type One Ventures and strategic investors including Cisco Investments and Samsung Catalyst Fund. This is evidence of participation at that date. It is not a present-day ranking of the largest shareholders, and BlackRock’s name does not mean its public company directly holds every investment attributed to its funds.

My comparison of the $2.8B and $6.9B financing values produces a roughly 2.46-fold increase. Both dates precede the Nvidia licensing and hiring agreement. A chart can preserve those two historical observations, but it cannot extend the $6.9B figure through the deal as if the business, workforce and rights were unchanged.

The difficult ownership question after the agreement is the perimeter of the remaining company. Who owns shares in Groq, which technology can Nvidia use, and which staff now work for the licensee are three different investigations. The public releases answer parts of the latter two. They do not provide an updated shareholder register, a distribution schedule or a complete valuation of Groq’s remaining operations.

This also changes how I read founder wealth headlines. Technology licence proceeds may be received and allocated under terms that are not public. A headline transaction value multiplied by an assumed founder stake would conceal those missing terms. I would need actual ownership, preferences, liabilities and the treatment of proceeds before reporting a personal estimate.

For readers comparing chip businesses, the public shareholder question explains ownership on the other side of this transaction. Groq’s private share access and Nvidia’s listed stock are separate instruments. Buying the licensee’s shares does not give an investor a direct registered holding in Groq.

founderStory: Groq’s financing release dates its founding to 2016 and identifies Jonathan Ross as founder and CEO at that time. The December release describes his move to Nvidia and names Simon Edwards to lead independent Groq. An old fundraising title should not be carried forward as a current executive title.

The licensing price does not establish Ross’s personal net worth. That calculation needs his actual interest, distribution rights, liabilities and other assets. Payments for workforce and technology rights need not become cash paid to a founder in proportion to a guessed stake. A future Ross profile should be sourced before it is linked here.
funding: The [September company release](source:groq-e) establishes a priced financing. The later licensing payment is a different transaction. Joining $6.9B to $17B in a rising valuation chart would compare unlike measures.

I retain the single verified financing observation and the transaction table. Earlier rounds can extend the chart after contemporaneous prices and terms are checked. The value of Groq’s continuing independent business is not established by Nvidia’s payment schedule.

A prospective investor also needs to understand how the transaction altered the business being purchased. Historical revenue, engineering capacity and product plans may not describe the residual operation on the same basis. A before-and-after comparison needs a clear perimeter, not merely a change in headline price.
files.chartRead: I read the two bars as pre-agreement funding benchmarks. The rise from $2.8B to $6.9B does not establish a post-licensing valuation for the remaining company.

timeline.ownerAfter: Independent private company per reviewed records

finding.heading: The $20B headline becomes a $13B-plus-$4B filing schedule
paragraphs: The annual report’s cash schedule totals $17B, including imputed interest in the amount payable. I use that documented figure rather than presenting an unverified approximately $20B headline as filed consideration.

My read: reconciling transaction type and payment timing is more useful than selecting the biggest number. Cash paid at closing and a future obligation differ. Neither establishes the company’s post-deal value or a payment to each individual shareholder.

Nvidia also records goodwill and developed technology. Accounting for a workforce and future development can involve goodwill even when no equity interests were purchased. Goodwill alone is therefore insufficient evidence that Groq became a subsidiary.

stock: No public Groq listing is established in the records checked. Buying Nvidia shares buys Nvidia’s wider business, not direct ownership of independent Groq. Private vehicles also require their own holdings, fee and share-class disclosures.

There is no substantiated Groq IPO date in these sources. The licence may alter the remaining company’s strategy, but I do not infer a listing schedule from it. [Lambda’s ownership investigation](/who-owns-lambda/) separates a reported IPO aim from completed financing, while [Crusoe’s company file](/who-owns-crusoe/) distinguishes initial closings from anticipated totals.

The ruling’s exchange mechanics do not establish those events. They also do not tell me each investor’s percentage after later transactions, so the holder table does not turn continuity at the restructuring date into an October 2026 cap table.

A pledge is meaningful intent, but a dated shareholder list and completed transfers would be needed to map legal ownership and votes. For a possible IPO, the parent-company change may remove a structural step from a future listing process. That is my interpretation of the corporate arrangement, not evidence that a registration statement has been filed or an offer priced. An employee liquidity transaction would likewise require its own date and terms rather than extending the old primary-round chart.

Incorporation and launch are different milestones: the ruling dates the old entity to 2012, while the [company timeline](source:canva-history) describes the design product’s development. I do not turn an incorporation date into the first-customer date.

A foundation pledge also differs from a current shareholder register. A philanthropic commitment does not, by itself, demonstrate that a specific number of shares and their votes have already transferred. Exact current founder holdings should be sourced before building personal net-worth estimates.

The investment question also depends on rights. A preferred holder may receive protections different from common shareholders or employee options. The sum invested divided by the headline company value is insufficient to establish a current percentage after later transactions.

The fully diluted stake is also not a personal founder estimate. The investor’s institutional interest belongs to the investor; the founder’s interest needs its own denominator and rights. Corporate valuation and founder wealth should not be substituted for one another.

paragraphs: ASML’s approximately 11% fully diluted interest is a disclosure tied to the September 2025 financing. The 2026 financing involves additional investors and fresh money. That alone is enough to require a fresh ownership calculation; it is not enough to perform one accurately. We would need ASML’s new subscription, any secondary transactions and the revised fully diluted share count.

The arithmetic is useful if its limits remain visible. Holding shares constant while increasing the company’s total shares would dilute a holder. Participating in a new issue could offset some or all of that dilution. We cannot choose between those paths from the fundraise headline, and the announcement’s inclusion of ASML as a participant still does not give its revised percentage.

The [current commercial terms](source:mistral-legal) identify a French corporation and a Paris registration number, while allowing an order form to specify an affiliate. That identifies the contracting framework. It does not show that Samsung, ASML or a cloud partner owns the operating entity outright, nor does it disclose the corporate group’s full shareholder register.

I also separate strategic governance from control. ASML’s advisory committee role has a disclosed purpose; it is not the same as a majority of board votes or the right to elect directors. Founder voting control needs the actual classes and constitutional arrangements. The public financing releases alone do not justify assigning such rights to either founders or investors.

founderStory: The [company history](source:mistral-about) dates Mistral’s beginning to April 2023 and names Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix as cofounders. Its current team page separates their jobs: CEO, Chief Science Officer and Chief Technology Officer. The key business question is why strategic industrial investors want exposure to the developer. A collaboration can support product use, research and a customer relationship while an equity investment supplies a separate financial interest. I would not read a product integration as proof of a larger shareholding than disclosed.

paragraphs: The [founder’s Series C account](source:glean-c) traces the product to a problem Arvind Jain encountered while building Rubrik: staff struggled to find knowledge scattered across workplace applications. ARR is also a recurring-revenue measure, rather than a cash balance, total contract value or audited revenue for a completed financial year. To evaluate the business behind the ownership story, I would want retention, gross margin, customer concentration and the conversion from bookings to recognized revenue. Those figures are not supplied by the valuation chart.

The [October fixed-rate financing](source:lambda-fixed) adds another clearly documented transaction: a delayed-draw facility of $1.008B in its highlights, priced at 6.78% with a final maturity in May 2033. The practical implication is that the financing stack cannot be reduced to a single total raised. Equity supplies ownership capital; debt supplies contractual funding with repayment obligations; customer contracts support the cash-flow story. Adding all three categories together would obscure the liabilities and ownership rights a stock investor actually needs to understand.

A facility rating is also narrower than a rating of every obligation of the parent company. Asset collateral, contract terms, maturity and amortization matter to that assessment. I report the facility’s terms with its own date, rather than using the investment-grade label to endorse a future equity offering.

The banks named in these releases arranged debt. Their presence does not verify the separate claim that banks have been hired for an IPO. The reported 2027 listing objective remains a plan, and the reported up-to-$4B equity raise remains proposed. Completed debt closings are important evidence of access to capital, but do not prove that those other transactions have closed.

extras.heading: Do Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan’s investments mean an IPO is booked?
paragraphs: The [company’s strategic-investment post](source:harvey-banks) establishes investment relationships. It does not, by itself, announce a dated IPO or establish that those organizations have been appointed to underwrite one.

Investment, customer use, financing advice and underwriting are different roles, sometimes carried out by different entities inside a financial group. An article should name the role supported by the actual release rather than infer all the others from a familiar bank brand.

That separation also applies to technology suppliers. Using models or integrating a productivity platform does not establish that the supplier owns the customer’s entire business. The ownership of [ChatGPT and OpenAI](/who-owns-chatgpt-openai/) is a separate investigation from ownership of an application that uses AI.

extras.heading: A legal information investor is not the owner of the whole platform
paragraphs: The [Series E announcement](source:harvey-e) identifies REV as the venture arm of RELX, whose businesses include LexisNexis. That is useful industry context: an established legal-information group participated in a legal AI financing. It does not establish that RELX acquired Harvey or that LexisNexis controls its board.

The July 2026 investment names Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and J.P. Morgan’s Growth Equity Partners. I use those precise investment-arm names instead of collapsing the transaction into a claim that either bank owns the entire company. The announcement confirms an investment, but does not disclose an ownership percentage or a new company valuation.

The [founders’ third-anniversary account](source:harvey-origin) also provides a dated origin checkpoint and identifies Siva Gurumurthy as CTO. This matters because a founder is often incorrectly assigned that title in summaries. Founding status, current management and present equity interests require separate records rather than a single inherited biography.

Adding the $5B Series E gives a longer sequence before the $11B and $15.5B financings. My first-to-last calculation is 3.1 times. The shorter March-to-September 2026 comparison is approximately 40.9%. These are changes in company funding benchmarks, not an increase in each founder’s personal liquid wealth.

A company can raise new money while individual shareholders are diluted, and a preferred-share price can differ economically from common stock. The relevant missing details are the fully diluted share count, preferences, vesting and any secondary sales. Those are the terms I would need to connect the funding chart to a founder’s actual economic exposure.

For the public-market question, investor participation is evidence of private capital backing. It does not produce a retail ticker or an announced listing date. A future IPO document could resolve holder percentages, voting rights and the proposed offering; until it exists, the ownership table shows disclosed relationships and keeps their undisclosed sizes visible.

The founder story is connected to legal workflow software, but the value of the entire platform is not the personal wealth of either founder. I would need holdings, classes, vesting, disposals and other assets and obligations before producing an individual estimate or a historical wealth chart.
